conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 refers to the mode as 'Lessons 3–6'. Lesson 3 covers the mean, Lesson 4 is the only mode lesson, and Lesson 5 covers the median.

conflicts.fact: Name and origin of the cumulative model students build
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 starts a 'Data Story Map' with frequency table. Lesson 2 says students revise a 'predictive model' of how to find the 'one best number'. Lesson 3 describes a 'Data Story Model' with the raw list added in L1 and the frequency table in L2. Lesson 5 calls it a 'Statistical Toolkit' started in Lesson 3. Lesson 4 calls it 'My Statistical Toolkit', a new comparison table.

conflicts.fact: Wording of the driving question on the DQB
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the board shows the Lesson 1 anchoring question: 'Which single number best represents all our farmers — and how do we even begin to make sense of all this data?'. Lessons 2, 3, 7 and 9 give the driving question as 'How can we collect, organize, and represent data about our community to help Kenyan decision-makers take effective action?'.

conflicts.fact: How the Nakuru frequency table is grouped into classes for graphs
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 groups the Nakuru data into six classes (1–5, 6–10, 11–15, 16–20, 21–25, 26–31) and says this is the Lesson 1 table. Lesson 1 lists each unique value with tallies. Lesson 8 regroups the same data into three ranges (1–10, 11–20, 21–31).
